comparator.name: Middle Eastern Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: Checked 2026-11-13. Actual current programme API, all 26 selected module payloads, seven-page programme OER, current faculty OER, public route/study pages and cohort-specific archive inspected. The formal route is Modern Middle East Studies; Arabic is the first listed language-package illustration, not a separate formal with-Arabic specialization. OER2.3 and public route require basic regional-language knowledge for MMO; advanced CEFR targets for Arabic/Persian/Turkish/Hebrew specializations are not MMO requirements. The 25 EC Arabic1/2/project sequence and Islam5 form the chosen30EC first-year package alongside30EC common study. Both Arabic2 and project require Arabic1 under OER4.2; module project also mentions instructor permission, not automatic formal waiver. Comparative Literatures10EC requires completed year one; additional all-BA2-language gate is limited to formal language specializations. Seminar5EC and thesis10EC both require completed year one and55ECyear two; current residual Philosophy-of-Science wording requires cohort clarification. Thesis uses supervised research, secondary literature and a bounded primary-source corpus; language-specialization primary-language/summary requirements do not transfer wholesale to MMO, whose summary is English. Distinct components remain60+60+55=175EC. Identical5852VCAAY code/id/uid is repeated; the 30EC elective space is already counted and is not a source of another5EC. Faculty3.1/3.2 requires150ECcompulsory+30ECfree choice: sufficient level, no required-curriculum overlap, approval except recognized30ECLeiden/Delft/Erasmus minors, noHonoursCollege credits. Programme3.2.9 restricts Islam:ReligionandSociety minor depending on specialization and abroad/shadow choice; no doublecount/automatic substitution. Current public pages give academic scope, not the missing replacement. The2025–26 archive explicitly separates entrant cohorts; its unused5ECchoice and approved individual shadow programme cannot be silently adopted for2026entrants. Current regulations listing has no adopted bridge; forward2271 returns current2261 bytes. All175EC and reusable research preserved; no no-match or approval. Stage 2 checked 17 November 2026: current BA-MOS-MMO/root and all 25 named module bodies rechecked; 26 components and 175 EC retained. Current formal programme OER and public route read through official-source web retrieval after direct public/PDF transport returned blocked HTML. Missing 5 EC and full cohort progression remain uncertified. Bounded negative judgment independently challenges actual UCR regional and comparative content with two full feasible 180-EC research trials; see docs/qc/evidence/qualified-comparison-stage2-2026-11-15/cp-000306/external-review.json.

exception.reason: UCR offers genuine regional connections in Arabic and Near Eastern narrative, Islamic Mediterranean artistic exchange and Persian imperial history, supported by substantial comparative political, social, economic and cultural inquiry. Its strongest feasible combinations do not sustain Middle Eastern societies and sources as the continuing object of historical, religious, political-economic, ethnographic and modern literary study. General comparative tools or hypothetical region-focused research do not create that taught regional progression. This is not a judgment based on missing language teaching alone.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Middle Eastern Studies bachelor examines the region’s history, societies, religions, languages and politics. This example follows the broad Modern Middle East Studies route, with basic Arabic language study.
audience.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for this documented Middle Eastern Studies curriculum. UCR has relevant regional literature, art and imperial history, alongside comparative social, political and economic study. Its strongest combinations do not sustain the degree’s continuing study of Middle Eastern societies, religions, politics and modern literature. The missing 5 EC and unresolved progression rules remain separate limitations.

curriculum.routeLabel: Modern Middle East Studies with Arabic
curriculum.limitation: The 175 EC shown include 30 EC of approved elective study and count History of Central Asia & Afghanistan once. Leiden’s guide repeats that course in years two and three. The remaining 5 EC and the application of seminar and thesis entry rules to this entrant cohort remain unverified.

componentNotes.curr-5853vewy: Entry requires completion of year one and 55 EC from year two. The thesis is written within the thesis seminar; the application of the entry rule to this entrant cohort remains under review.
componentNotes.curr-component-26: 30 EC in the first semester of year three for elective study of sufficient level without overlap with required courses. Examination-board approval applies except for recognized 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus. Programme-specific minor restrictions also apply; Honours College courses cannot fill this space.

componentNotes.curr-5853vsmosy: Entry requires completion of year one and 55 EC from year two. The application of the published rule to this entrant cohort remains under review.
